messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with Axis Ticks
parts:
Add, library(grid)

unit() is part of that package. I'm surprised by this. I know ggplot2 has stripped things away, but I didn't realize that it was quite this stripped down. 



On Mon, Jun 25, 2012 at 1:31 PM, Lorenzo Isella <lorenzo...@gmail.com> wrote:
library(ggplot2)

mydata <- as.data.frame(cbind(seq(10), seq(10)))


names(mydata) <- c("ratio", "N")

b <- ggplot(mydata, aes(x=N, y=ratio))  +

 geom_point(size=2) +

 opts( panel.background=theme_rect(fill='white',
                  size=1.5))+
  opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
  opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
     opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black", size=1)
          , axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm")
          )

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with Axis Ticks
parts:
I believe this has to do with ggplot2 not autoloading packages at
startup as of 0.9.0. Just as you now have to explicitly load plyr and
reshape if you want to use them in a session, so too do you have to
load grid. Every once in a while you forget and get nipped...

Dennis
